To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the GATS does not adequately address digital services trade and the e commerce chapters in PTAs do not fill the gaps; (ii) PTAs do not address all barriers to digital services, but focus on specific barriers, such as data localisation and cross border data flows; and (iii) the e commerce chapters are not only about e commerce but also about digital services trade, as they address barriers to digital services that are not related to e commerce.
the GATS framework is applicable to digital services and that the e commerce chapters are not addressing all barriers to digital services.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) To what extent is the GATS framework applicable to digital services trade?
the question of whether PTAs can be used to address the gaps in the current multilateral rules and, if so, whether they do so.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the digital services trade agenda has been addressed only in the 11 ^{th} hour in PTAs.
the e commerce chapters are not yet addressing all the barriers to digital services identified in the GATS.
the GATS is not a comprehensive enough framework for digital services trade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
digital services are being addressed in PTAs, but that there is a lack of convergence on digital services trade issues in the 11 ^{th} hour.
the e commerce chapter is not a substitute for the GATS.
there is a clear convergence in PTAs on the e commerce related content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
digital services trade is not addressed in the vast majority of PTAs, and the few that do address digital services trade do so in a limited way.
PTAs have the potential to address the gaps in the GATS and to fill the gaps left by the e commerce chapter of the CPTPP.
PTAs have been slow in addressing barriers to the digital trade of services, and the few PTAs that do address them have done so in the last couple of years.
